title: Senior Intraoperative Neuromonitoring (IOM) Technologist - Full Time - Days

cond_0001.intro: The Senior Intraoperative Neuromonitoring (IOM) Technologist is responsible for performing neurodiagnostic procedures in the intraoperative monitoring field and all IOM modalities required as a registered neurodiagnostic technologist. In addition to performing the duties of the IOM Technologist, this position independently performs IOM modalities including SSEPs, TceMEP, EMG (including triggered), ABRs, Phase Reversal, and cortical mapping. When not scheduled for an IOM case, the Senior IOM Technologist may be asked to perform ambulatory and long term monitoring (LTM) electroencephalograms (EEG), and/or visual, brainstem, and somatosensory evoked potential (EP) procedures and/or monitor epilepsy patients according to hospital and departmental policy and procedures. This position delivers exceptional patient care per guidelines established by the department to ensure optimal patient safety and customer service and practices Patient and Family-Centered Care.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
People Essential Functions
Ensures understanding by the patient and staff the purpose of the procedures and answers questions regarding the procedures. Identifies and anticipates potential problems, communicates appropriately and effectively concerns to appropriate management; addresses issues as instructed, responding professionally at all times, and reports resolutions. Role models' healthy work relationships such as mitigation of conflict, leading problem-solving and resolution efforts. Anticipates needs of other team members; proactively offers assistance and promotes a positive work environment that actively assists interprofessional care team to achieve optimal department results. Serves as preceptor, mentor, and resource to less experience staff. Provides technical expertise to peers and/or non-credentialed team members as appropriate. Recommends initiatives to improve department scores for employee engagement on department scorecard.
Service Essential Functions
Independently conducts patient assessments. Recognizes and teaches peers drug and physiological status effects on activity monitored. In addition to performing all IOM modalities, independently performs EEG monitoring during: Wada, PET, ictal SPECT studies, ABRs, Phase Reversal and cortical mapping with indirect supervision as appropriate. Conducts intermediate to advanced technical troubleshooting and artifact identification and elimination; understands and follows concepts of digital equipment and electrical safety with regards to the equipment. Shares understanding with peers of EEG technology and its uses in the epilepsy monitoring unit as well as during epilepsy surgery. Independently monitors epilepsy monitoring patients. Independently performs EP studies or other EEG studies as assigned when there are no scheduled IOM cases. Role models behaviors and skills, through peer-to-peer accountability, towards improving department score for patient satisfaction.
Quality/Safety Essential Functions
Identifies clinically significant events and follows policy and procedure regarding critical test results, maintaining the patient's safety through communication to other patient care support staff during these procedures as appropriate. Identifies and assesses issues and opportunities for improvement and implements changes following managerial review. Follows up on action items to ensure completion. Contributes towards improving quality and safety scores on department scorecard.
Finance Essential Functions
Charges accurately for procedures, and logging the patient data. Submits all reports, billing and other paperwork within a timely manner. Uses resources efficiently; does not waste supplies. Ensures inventories of major supplies are never depleted. Self-motivated to independently manage time effectively and prioritize daily tasks, minimizing incidental overtime.
Growth/Innovation Essential Functions
Continues to learn and apply intermediate to advanced EEG and/or EP signal recognition, relevant medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, contraindications for activation procedures, instrumentation and preparation for use. Trains in END procedures. Offers innovative solutions through participation in performance improvement activities. Completes and updates the individual development plan (IDP) on an on-going basis.
This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive; the employee will also perform other reasonably related business/job duties as assigned. [Company name masked] reserves the right to revise job duties and responsibilities as the need arises.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High School diploma or equivalent education (examples include: GED, verification of homeschool equivalency, partial or full completion of post-secondary education, etc.), completion of an Accredited Electroneurodiagnostic (END) program, or Associate's degree or higher in a science related field from an accredited college or university
Two years experience in IOM procedures
Preferred Requirements
Associate's degree or higher in a science related field from an accredited college or university
Completion of an Accredited Electroneurodiagnostic (END) program

In addition to performing the duties of the IOM Technologist, this position independently performs IOM modalities including SSEPs, TceMEP, EMG (including triggered), ABRs, Phase Reversal, and cortical mapping. When not scheduled for an IOM case, the Senior IOM Technologist may be asked to perform ambulatory and long term monitoring (LTM) electroencephalograms (EEG), and/or visual, brainstem, and somatosensory evoked potential (EP) procedures and/or monitor epilepsy patients according to hospital and departmental policy and procedures. This position delivers exceptional patient care per guidelines established by the department to ensure optimal patient safety and customer service and practices Patient and Family-Centered Care.
cond_0092.responsibilities:
People Essential Functions
Ensures understanding by the patient and staff the purpose of the procedures and answers questions regarding the procedures. Identifies and anticipates potential problems, communicates appropriately and effectively concerns to appropriate management; addresses issues as instructed, responding professionally at all times, and reports resolutions. Role models' healthy work relationships such as mitigation of conflict, leading problem-solving and resolution efforts. Anticipates needs of other team members; proactively offers assistance and promotes a positive work environment that actively assists interprofessional care team to achieve optimal department results. Serves as preceptor, mentor, and resource to less experience staff. Provides technical expertise to peers and/or non-credentialed team members as appropriate. Recommends initiatives to improve department scores for employee engagement on department scorecard.
Service Essential Functions
Independently conducts patient assessments. Recognizes and teaches peers drug and physiological status effects on activity monitored. In addition to performing all IOM modalities, independently performs EEG monitoring during: Wada, PET, ictal SPECT studies, ABRs, Phase Reversal and cortical mapping with indirect supervision as appropriate. Conducts intermediate to advanced technical troubleshooting and artifact identification and elimination; understands and follows concepts of digital equipment and electrical safety with regards to the equipment. Shares understanding with peers of EEG technology and its uses in the epilepsy monitoring unit as well as during epilepsy surgery. Independently monitors epilepsy monitoring patients. Independently performs EP studies or other EEG studies as assigned when there are no scheduled IOM cases. Role models behaviors and skills, through peer-to-peer accountability, towards improving department score for patient satisfaction.
Quality/Safety Essential Functions
Identifies clinically significant events and follows policy and procedure regarding critical test results, maintaining the patient's safety through communication to other patient care support staff during these procedures as appropriate. Identifies and assesses issues and opportunities for improvement and implements changes following managerial review. Follows up on action items to ensure completion. Contributes towards improving quality and safety scores on department scorecard.
Finance Essential Functions
Charges accurately for procedures, and logging the patient data. Submits all reports, billing and other paperwork within a timely manner. Uses resources efficiently; does not waste supplies. Ensures inventories of major supplies are never depleted. Self-motivated to independently manage time effectively and prioritize daily tasks, minimizing incidental overtime.
Growth/Innovation Essential Functions
Continues to learn and apply intermediate to advanced EEG and/or EP signal recognition, relevant medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, contraindications for activation procedures, instrumentation and preparation for use. Trains in END procedures. Offers innovative solutions through participation in performance improvement activities. Completes and updates the individual development plan (IDP) on an on-going basis.
This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive; the employee will also perform other reasonably related business/job duties as assigned. [Company name masked] reserves the right to revise job duties and responsibilities as the need arises.
cond_0092.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Demonstrated expertise in IOM procedures, with a minimum of two years of proven, hands-on experience in the field
Advanced knowledge of IOM modalities including SSEPs, TceMEP, EMG (including triggered), ABRs, Phase Reversal, and cortical mapping
Must hold one of the following: High School diploma or equivalent, completion of an accredited Electroneurodiagnostic (END) program, or an Associate's degree or higher in a science-related field from an accredited college or university
Preferred Requirements
Associate's degree or higher in a science-related field; advanced degree strongly preferred
Deep knowledge of EEG technology and its application in epilepsy monitoring and epilepsy surgery settings
Strong command of intermediate to advanced technical troubleshooting, artifact identification and elimination, and digital equipment and electrical safety concepts
Proficiency in EEG signal recognition, relevant medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, and contraindications for activation procedures
Exceptional communication skills and strong leadership abilities, with the ability to serve as a preceptor and mentor to less experienced staff

Together with the team, you will help ensure optimal patient safety and customer service, and support Patient and Family-Centered Care. When not scheduled for an IOM case, you may be asked to assist with ambulatory and long-term monitoring (LTM) electroencephalograms (EEG), visual, brainstem, and somatosensory evoked potential (EP) procedures, and/or monitoring of epilepsy patients in accordance with hospital and departmental policies.

cond_0136.intro: At [Company name masked], the Senior Intraoperative Neuromonitoring (IOM) Technologist is responsible for performing neurodiagnostic procedures in the intraoperative monitoring field as well as all IOM modalities required as a registered neurodiagnostic technologist. In addition to performing the duties of the IOM Technologist, this position independently performs IOM modalities including SSEPs, TceMEP, EMG (including triggered), ABRs, Phase Reversal and cortical mapping. When not scheduled for an IOM case, the Senior IOM Technologist may be asked to perform ambulatory and long term monitoring (LTM) electroencephalograms (EEG), and/or visual, brainstem, and somatosensory evoked potential (EP) procedures and/or monitor epilepsy patients according to hospital and departmental policy and procedures. This position delivers exceptional patient care per guidelines established by the department to ensure optimal patient safety and customer service and practices Patient and Family-Centered Care.
cond_0136.responsibilities:
People Essential Functions
Ensures understanding by the patient and staff the purpose of the procedures and answers questions regarding the procedures. Identifies and anticipates potential problems, communicates appropriately and effectively concerns to appropriate management; addresses issues as instructed, responding professionally at all times, and reports resolutions. Role models' healthy work relationships such as mitigation of conflict, leading problem-solving and resolution efforts. Anticipates needs of other team members; proactively offers assistance and promotes a positive work environment that actively assists interprofessional care team to achieve optimal department results. Serves as preceptor, mentor, and resource to less experience staff. Provides technical expertise to peers and/or non-credentialed team members as appropriate. Recommends initiatives to improve department scores for employee engagement on department scorecard.
Service Essential Functions
Independently conducts patient assessments. Recognizes and teaches peers drug and physiological status effects on activity monitored. In addition to performing all IOM modalities, independently performs EEG monitoring during: Wada, PET, ictal SPECT studies, ABRs, Phase Reversal and cortical mapping with indirect supervision as appropriate. Conducts intermediate to advanced technical troubleshooting and artifact identification and elimination; understands and follows concepts of digital equipment and electrical safety with regards to the equipment. Shares understanding with peers of EEG technology and its uses in the epilepsy monitoring unit as well as during epilepsy surgery. Independently monitors epilepsy monitoring patients. Independently performs EP studies or other EEG studies as assigned when there are no scheduled IOM cases. Role models behaviors and skills, through peer-to-peer accountability, towards improving department score for patient satisfaction.
Quality/Safety Essential Functions
Identifies clinically significant events and follows policy and procedure regarding critical test results, maintaining the patient's safety through communication to other patient care support staff during these procedures as appropriate. Identifies and assesses issues and opportunities for improvement and implements changes following managerial review. Follows up on action items to ensure completion. Contributes towards improving quality and safety scores on department scorecard.
Finance Essential Functions
Charges accurately for procedures, and logging the patient data. Submits all reports, billing and other paperwork within a timely manner. Uses resources efficiently; does not waste supplies. Ensures inventories of major supplies are never depleted. Self-motivated to independently manage time effectively and prioritize daily tasks, minimizing incidental overtime.
Growth/Innovation Essential Functions
Continues to learn and apply intermediate to advanced EEG and/or EP signal recognition, relevant medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, contraindications for activation procedures, instrumentation and preparation for use. Trains in END procedures. Offers innovative solutions through participation in performance improvement activities. Completes and updates the individual development plan (IDP) on an on-going basis.
This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive; the employee will also perform other reasonably related business/job duties as assigned. [Company name masked] reserves the right to revise job duties and responsibilities as the need arises.
cond_0136.requirements:
Must have one of the following: High School diploma or equivalent education (examples include: GED, verification of homeschool equivalency, partial or full completion of post-secondary education, etc.), Completion of an Accredited Electroneurodiagnostic (END) program, or Associate's degree or higher in a science related field from an accredited college or university
Two years experience in IOM procedures

cond_0179.intro: At [Company name masked], the Senior Intraoperative Neuromonitoring (IOM) Technologist owns the full scope of neurodiagnostic procedures in the intraoperative monitoring field, executing all IOM modalities required as a registered neurodiagnostic technologist. Beyond core IOM duties, this role independently executes IOM modalities including SSEPs, TceMEP, EMG (including triggered), ABRs, Phase Reversal, and cortical mapping. When not scheduled for an IOM case, the Senior IOM Technologist may be directed to perform ambulatory and long-term monitoring (LTM) electroencephalograms (EEG), and/or visual, brainstem, and somatosensory evoked potential (EP) procedures and/or monitor epilepsy patients according to hospital and departmental policy and procedures. This position delivers exceptional patient care per guidelines established by the department to ensure optimal patient safety and customer service and practices Patient and Family-Centered Care.
cond_0179.responsibilities:
People Essential Functions
Ensures understanding by the patient and staff of the purpose of procedures and answers questions regarding the procedures. Identifies and anticipates potential problems, communicates concerns effectively to appropriate management, addresses issues as instructed, responding professionally at all times, and reports resolutions. Leads healthy work relationships such as mitigation of conflict, driving problem-solving and resolution efforts. Anticipates needs of other team members; proactively offers assistance and promotes a positive work environment that actively assists the interprofessional care team to achieve optimal department results. Serves as preceptor, mentor, and resource to less experienced staff. Delivers technical expertise to peers and/or non-credentialed team members as appropriate. Recommends initiatives to improve department scores for employee engagement on department scorecard.
Service Essential Functions
Independently conducts patient assessments. Recognizes and teaches peers drug and physiological status effects on activity monitored. In addition to performing all IOM modalities, independently executes EEG monitoring during: Wada, PET, ictal SPECT studies, ABRs, Phase Reversal, and cortical mapping with indirect supervision as appropriate. Conducts intermediate to advanced technical troubleshooting and artifact identification and elimination; understands and follows concepts of digital equipment and electrical safety with regards to the equipment. Shares understanding with peers of EEG technology and its uses in the epilepsy monitoring unit as well as during epilepsy surgery. Independently monitors epilepsy monitoring patients. Independently performs EP studies or other EEG studies as assigned when there are no scheduled IOM cases. Models behaviors and skills, through peer-to-peer accountability, toward improving department score for patient satisfaction.
Quality/Safety Essential Functions
Identifies clinically significant events and follows policy and procedure regarding critical test results, maintaining the patient's safety through communication to other patient care support staff during these procedures as appropriate. Identifies and assesses issues and opportunities for improvement and implements changes following managerial review. Follows up on action items to ensure completion. Contributes toward improving quality and safety scores on department scorecard.
Finance Essential Functions
Charges accurately for procedures and logs patient data. Submits all reports, billing, and other paperwork in a timely manner. Uses resources efficiently; does not waste supplies. Ensures inventories of major supplies are never depleted. Independently manages time effectively and prioritizes daily tasks, minimizing incidental overtime.
Growth/Innovation Essential Functions
Continues to learn and apply intermediate to advanced EEG and/or EP signal recognition, relevant medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, contraindications for activation procedures, instrumentation, and preparation for use. Trains in END procedures. Offers innovative solutions through participation in performance improvement activities. Completes and updates the individual development plan (IDP) on an ongoing basis.
This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive; the employee will also perform other reasonably related business/job duties as assigned. [Company name masked] reserves the right to revise job duties and responsibilities as the need arises.
cond_0179.requirements:
Must have one of the following: High School diploma or equivalent education (examples include: GED, verification of homeschool equivalency, partial or full completion of post-secondary education, etc.), Completion of an Accredited Electroneurodiagnostic (END) program, or Associate's degree or higher in a science related field from an accredited college or university
Two years experience in IOM procedures

Ensure patients and staff understand the purpose of procedures and answer questions about them. Identify and anticipate potential problems, communicate concerns to appropriate management, address issues as instructed, respond professionally at all times, and report resolutions. Model healthy work relationships including conflict mitigation and leading problem-solving and resolution efforts. Anticipate team members' needs, proactively offer assistance, and foster a positive work environment that actively supports the interprofessional care team in achieving optimal department results. Serve as preceptor, mentor, and resource to less experienced staff. Deliver technical expertise to peers and/or non-credentialed team members as appropriate. Recommend initiatives to improve department employee engagement scores on the department scorecard.
Service Essential Functions
Independently conduct patient assessments. Recognize and teach peers about drug and physiological status effects on monitored activity. In addition to executing all IOM modalities, independently perform EEG monitoring during: Wada, PET, ictal SPECT studies, ABRs, Phase Reversal, and cortical mapping with indirect supervision as appropriate. Lead intermediate to advanced technical troubleshooting and artifact identification and elimination; understand and apply concepts of digital equipment and electrical safety with regards to the equipment. Share understanding with peers of EEG technology and its uses in the epilepsy monitoring unit and during epilepsy surgery. Independently monitor epilepsy monitoring patients. Independently perform EP studies or other EEG studies as assigned when there are no scheduled IOM cases. Model behaviors and skills through peer-to-peer accountability toward improving department patient satisfaction scores.
Quality/Safety Essential Functions
Identify clinically significant events and follow policy and procedure regarding critical test results, maintaining patient safety through communication to other patient care support staff during procedures as appropriate. Identify and assess issues and opportunities for improvement and implement changes following managerial review. Follow up on action items to ensure completion. Contribute toward improving quality and safety scores on the department scorecard.
Finance Essential Functions
Charge accurately for procedures and log patient data. Submit all reports, billing, and other paperwork in a timely manner. Use resources efficiently and avoid wasting supplies. Ensure inventories of major supplies are never depleted. Independently manage time effectively and prioritize daily tasks, minimizing incidental overtime.
Growth/Innovation Essential Functions
Continue to learn and apply intermediate to advanced EEG and/or EP signal recognition, relevant medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, contraindications for activation procedures, instrumentation, and preparation for use. Train in END procedures. Offer innovative solutions through participation in performance improvement activities. Complete and update the individual development plan (IDP) on an ongoing basis.
This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive; the employee will also perform other reasonably related business/job duties as assigned. [Company name masked] reserves the right to revise job duties and responsibilities as the need arises.
cond_0224.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Must have one of the following: High School diploma or equivalent education (examples include: GED, verification of homeschool equivalency, partial or full completion of post-secondary education, etc.), completion of an Accredited Electroneurodiagnostic (END) program, or Associate's degree or higher in a science-related field from an accredited college or university
Two years of experience in IOM procedures
Preferred Requirements
Associate's degree or higher in a science-related field from an accredited college or university (if not already used to satisfy the minimum education requirement)
Completion of an Accredited Electroneurodiagnostic (END) program (if not already used to satisfy the minimum education requirement)

cond_0225.intro:
We are looking for a Senior Intraoperative Neuromonitoring (IOM) Technologist to join our team.
In this role, you will work alongside clinical and interprofessional teams to support neurodiagnostic procedures in the intraoperative monitoring field, covering all IOM modalities required of a registered neurodiagnostic technologist. Together with the team, you will help ensure optimal patient safety and customer service, and support Patient and Family-Centered Care. When not scheduled for an IOM case, you may be asked to assist with ambulatory and long-term monitoring (LTM) electroencephalograms (EEG), visual, brainstem, and somatosensory evoked potential (EP) procedures, and/or monitoring of epilepsy patients in accordance with hospital and departmental policies.
cond_0225.responsibilities:
People Essential Functions
Help patients and staff understand the purpose of procedures and answer their questions. Identify and anticipate potential problems, share concerns with appropriate management in a timely and professional manner, and follow through on resolutions as directed. Support healthy work relationships by helping to address conflict and contributing to problem-solving efforts. Anticipate the needs of team members, offer assistance proactively, and help foster a positive environment that supports the interprofessional care team in achieving department goals. Serve as preceptor, mentor, and resource to less experienced staff. Share technical expertise with peers and non-credentialed team members as appropriate. Contribute ideas to improve employee engagement scores on the department scorecard.
Service Essential Functions
Conduct patient assessments and help peers recognize drug and physiological status effects on monitored activity. In addition to supporting all IOM modalities, assist with EEG monitoring during Wada, PET, ictal SPECT studies, ABRs, Phase Reversal, and cortical mapping with appropriate supervision. Contribute to intermediate to advanced technical troubleshooting and artifact identification and elimination; follow concepts of digital equipment and electrical safety. Share knowledge of EEG technology and its uses in the epilepsy monitoring unit and during epilepsy surgery. Support epilepsy monitoring patients and assist with EP studies or other EEG studies as assigned when no IOM cases are scheduled. Model behaviors and skills through peer-to-peer accountability to help improve patient satisfaction scores.
Quality/Safety Essential Functions
Identify clinically significant events and follow policy and procedure regarding critical test results, helping to maintain patient safety through communication with care support staff during procedures. Identify issues and opportunities for improvement and help implement changes following managerial review. Follow up on action items to ensure completion. Contribute to improving quality and safety scores on the department scorecard.
Finance Essential Functions
Charge accurately for procedures and log patient data. Submit all reports, billing, and other paperwork in a timely manner. Use resources efficiently and avoid wasting supplies. Help ensure inventories of major supplies are maintained. Manage time effectively and prioritize daily tasks to minimize incidental overtime.
Growth/Innovation Essential Functions
Continue to develop and apply intermediate to advanced EEG and/or EP signal recognition, relevant medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, contraindications for activation procedures, instrumentation, and preparation for use. Train in END procedures. Contribute innovative solutions through participation in performance improvement activities. Complete and update the individual development plan (IDP) on an ongoing basis.
This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive; the employee will also perform other reasonably related business/job duties as assigned. [Company name masked] reserves the right to revise job duties and responsibilities as the need arises.
cond_0225.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Must have one of the following: High School diploma or equivalent education (examples include: GED, verification of homeschool equivalency, partial or full completion of post-secondary education, etc.), completion of an Accredited Electroneurodiagnostic (END) program, or Associate's degree or higher in a science-related field from an accredited college or university
Two years of experience in IOM procedures
Preferred Requirements
Proficiency in independently performing IOM modalities including SSEPs, TceMEP, EMG (including triggered), ABRs, Phase Reversal, and cortical mapping
Experience with ambulatory and long-term monitoring (LTM) EEG, and/or visual, brainstem, and somatosensory evoked potential (EP) procedures
Intermediate to advanced EEG and/or EP signal recognition skills

In addition to performing the duties of the IOM Technologist, this position is efficient in independently performing IOM modalities including SSEPs, TceMEP, EMG (including triggered), ABR's, Phase Reversal and cortical mapping. When not scheduled for an IOM case, the Senior IOM Technologist may be asked to perform ambulatory and long term monitoring (LTM) electroencephalograms (EEG), and/or visual, brainstem, and somatosensory evoked potential (EP) procedures and/or monitor epilepsy patients according to hospital and departmental policy and procedures. This position delivers exceptional patient care per guidelines established by the department to ensure optimal patient safety and customer service and practices Patient and Family-Centered Care. People tend to become stronger in this kind of neuromonitoring work over time as they build experience across different modalities and clinical settings.
cond_0266.responsibilities:
People Essential Functions
Ensures understanding by the patient and staff the purpose of the procedures and answers questions regarding the procedures. Identifies and anticipates potential problems, communicates appropriately and effectively concerns to appropriate management; addresses issues as instructed, responding professionally at all times, and reports resolutions. Role models' healthy work relationships such as mitigation of conflict, leading problem-solving and resolution efforts. Anticipates needs of other team members; proactively offers assistance and promotes a positive work environment that actively assists interprofessional care team to achieve optimal department results. Serves as preceptor, mentor, and resource to less experience staff. Provides technical expertise to peers and/or non-credentialed team members as appropriate. Recommends initiatives to improve department scores for employee engagement on department scorecard.
Service Essential Functions
Independently conducts patient assessments. Recognizes and teaches peers drug and physiological status effects on activity monitored. In addition to performing all IOM modalities, independently performs EEG monitoring during: Wada, PET, ictal SPECT studies, ABRs, Phase Reversal and cortical mapping with indirect supervision as appropriate. Conducts intermediate to advanced technical troubleshooting and artifact identification and elimination; understands and follows concepts of digital equipment and electrical safety with regards to the equipment. Shares understanding with peers of EEG technology and its uses in the epilepsy monitoring unit as well as during epilepsy surgery. Independently monitors epilepsy monitoring patients. Independently performs EP studies or other EEG studies as assigned when there are no scheduled IOM cases. Role models behaviors and skills, through peer-to-peer accountability, towards improving department score for patient satisfaction.
Quality/Safety Essential Functions
Identifies clinically significant events and follows policy and procedure regarding critical test results, maintaining the patient's safety through communication to other patient care support staff during these procedures as appropriate. Identifies and assesses issues and opportunities for improvement and implements changes following managerial review. Follows up on action items to ensure completion. Contributes towards improving quality and safety scores on department scorecard.
Finance Essential Functions
Charges accurately for procedures, and logging the patient data. Submits all reports, billing and other paperwork within a timely manner. Uses resources efficiently; does not waste supplies. Ensures inventories of major supplies are never depleted. Self-motivated to independently manage time effectively and prioritize daily tasks, minimizing incidental overtime.
Growth/Innovation Essential Functions
Continues to learn and apply intermediate to advanced EEG and/or EP signal recognition, relevant medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, contraindications for activation procedures, instrumentation and preparation for use. Trains in END procedures. Offers innovative solutions through participation in performance improvement activities. Completes and updates the individual development plan (IDP) on an on-going basis.
This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive; the employee will also perform other reasonably related business/job duties as assigned. [Company name masked] reserves the right to revise job duties and responsibilities as the need arises.
cond_0266.requirements:
Must have one of the following: High School diploma or equivalent education (examples include: GED, verification of homeschool equivalency, partial or full completion of post-secondary education, etc.), Completion of an Accredited Electroneurodiagnostic (END) program, or Associate's degree or higher in a science related field from an accredited college or university
Two years experience in IOM procedures

cond_0294.intro: At [Company name masked], the Senior Intraoperative Neuromonitoring (IOM) Technologist is responsible for performing neurodiagnostic procedures in the intraoperative monitoring field and all IOM modalities required as a registered neurodiagnostic technologist. This position independently performs IOM modalities including SSEPs, TceMEP, EMG (including triggered), ABRs, Phase Reversal, and cortical mapping. When not scheduled for an IOM case, the Senior IOM Technologist may be asked to perform ambulatory and long-term monitoring (LTM) electroencephalograms (EEG), and/or visual, brainstem, and somatosensory evoked potential (EP) procedures, and/or monitor epilepsy patients according to hospital and departmental policy and procedures. This position delivers exceptional patient care per department guidelines to ensure optimal patient safety and customer service, and practices Patient and Family-Centered Care.
cond_0294.responsibilities:
People Essential Functions
Regularly communicates with patients and staff to ensure they understand the purpose of procedures, and actively answers their questions. Identifies and anticipates potential problems, communicates concerns clearly and promptly to appropriate management, addresses issues as instructed, responds professionally at all times, and reports resolutions. Models healthy work relationships including conflict mitigation, and leads problem-solving and resolution efforts. Anticipates needs of other team members, proactively offers assistance, and actively supports the interprofessional care team to achieve optimal department results. Serves as preceptor, mentor, and resource to less experienced staff. Provides technical expertise to peers and/or non-credentialed team members as appropriate. Recommends initiatives to improve department scores for employee engagement on department scorecard.
Service Essential Functions
Independently conducts patient assessments. Recognizes and teaches peers about drug and physiological status effects on monitored activity. In addition to performing all IOM modalities, independently performs EEG monitoring during: Wada, PET, ictal SPECT studies, ABRs, Phase Reversal, and cortical mapping with indirect supervision as appropriate. Conducts intermediate to advanced technical troubleshooting and artifact identification and elimination; understands and follows concepts of digital equipment and electrical safety with regards to the equipment. Actively shares understanding with peers of EEG technology and its uses in the epilepsy monitoring unit as well as during epilepsy surgery. Independently monitors epilepsy monitoring patients. Independently performs EP studies or other EEG studies as assigned when there are no scheduled IOM cases. Models behaviors and skills through peer-to-peer accountability toward improving department scores for patient satisfaction.
Quality/Safety Essential Functions
Identifies clinically significant events and follows policy and procedure regarding critical test results, maintaining patient safety through clear communication with other patient care support staff during these procedures as appropriate. Identifies and assesses issues and opportunities for improvement and implements changes following managerial review. Follows up on action items to ensure completion. Contributes toward improving quality and safety scores on department scorecard.
Finance Essential Functions
Charges accurately for procedures and logs patient data. Submits all reports, billing, and other paperwork in a timely manner. Uses resources efficiently and does not waste supplies. Ensures inventories of major supplies are never depleted. Independently manages time effectively and prioritizes daily tasks, minimizing incidental overtime.
Growth/Innovation Essential Functions
Continues to learn and apply intermediate to advanced EEG and/or EP signal recognition, relevant medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, contraindications for activation procedures, instrumentation, and preparation for use. Trains in END procedures. Offers innovative solutions through participation in performance improvement activities. Completes and updates the individual development plan (IDP) on an ongoing basis.
This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive; the employee will also perform other reasonably related business/job duties as assigned. [Company name masked] reserves the right to revise job duties and responsibilities as the need arises.

Minimum Requirements
Must have one of the following: High School diploma or equivalent education (examples include: GED, verification of homeschool equivalency, partial or full completion of post-secondary education, etc.), completion of an Accredited Electroneurodiagnostic (END) program, or Associate's degree or higher in a science-related field from an accredited college or university
Two years of experience in IOM procedures
Preferred Requirements
Proficiency in independently performing a broad range of IOM modalities including SSEPs, TceMEP, EMG (including triggered), ABRs, Phase Reversal, and cortical mapping

In this role, you will work alongside clinical and interprofessional teams to support neurodiagnostic procedures in the intraoperative monitoring field, covering all IOM modalities required of a registered neurodiagnostic technologist. Together with the team, you will help ensure optimal patient safety and customer service, and support Patient and Family-Centered Care. When not scheduled for an IOM case, you may be asked to assist with ambulatory and long-term monitoring (LTM) electroencephalograms (EEG), visual, brainstem, and somatosensory evoked potential (EP) procedures, and/or monitoring of epilepsy patients in accordance with hospital and departmental policies.

Contribute ideas to improve employee engagement scores on the department scorecard.

Conduct patient assessments and help peers recognize drug and physiological status effects on monitored activity. Contribute to intermediate to advanced technical troubleshooting and artifact identification and elimination; follow concepts of digital equipment and electrical safety. Share knowledge of EEG technology and its uses in the epilepsy monitoring unit and during epilepsy surgery. Support epilepsy monitoring patients and assist with EP studies or other EEG studies as assigned when no IOM cases are scheduled. Model behaviors and skills through peer-to-peer accountability to help improve patient satisfaction scores.
Quality/Safety Essential Functions
Identify clinically significant events and follow policy and procedure regarding critical test results, helping to maintain patient safety through communication with care support staff during procedures. Identify issues and opportunities for improvement and help implement changes following managerial review. Follow up on action items to ensure completion. Contribute to improving quality and safety scores on the department scorecard.
Finance Essential Functions
Charge accurately for procedures and log patient data. Submit all reports, billing, and other paperwork in a timely manner. Use resources efficiently and avoid wasting supplies. Help ensure inventories of major supplies are maintained. Manage time effectively and prioritize daily tasks to minimize incidental overtime.
Growth/Innovation Essential Functions
Continue to develop and apply intermediate to advanced EEG and/or EP signal recognition, relevant medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, contraindications for activation procedures, instrumentation, and preparation for use. Train in END procedures. Contribute innovative solutions through participation in performance improvement activities. Complete and update the individual development plan (IDP) on an ongoing basis.

Ensures understanding by the patient and staff the purpose of the procedures and answers questions regarding the procedures. Identifies and anticipates potential problems, communicates appropriately and effectively concerns to appropriate management; addresses issues as instructed, responding professionally at all times, and reports resolutions. Role models' healthy work relationships such as mitigation of conflict, leading problem-solving and resolution efforts. Anticipates needs of other team members; proactively offers assistance and promotes a positive work environment that actively assists interprofessional care team to achieve optimal department results. Serves as preceptor, mentor, and resource to less experience staff. Provides technical expertise to peers and/or non-credentialed team members as appropriate. Recommends initiatives to improve department scores for employee engagement on department scorecard.
Service Essential Functions
Independently conducts patient assessments. Recognizes and teaches peers drug and physiological status effects on activity monitored. In addition to performing all IOM modalities, independently performs EEG monitoring during: Wada, PET, ictal SPECT studies, ABRs, Phase Reversal and cortical mapping with indirect supervision as appropriate. Conducts intermediate to advanced technical troubleshooting and artifact identification and elimination; understands and follows concepts of digital equipment and electrical safety with regards to the equipment. Shares understanding with peers of EEG technology and its uses in the epilepsy monitoring unit as well as during epilepsy surgery. Independently monitors epilepsy monitoring patients. Independently performs EP studies or other EEG studies as assigned when there are no scheduled IOM cases. Role models behaviors and skills, through peer-to-peer accountability, towards improving department score for patient satisfaction.
Quality/Safety Essential Functions
Identifies clinically significant events and follows policy and procedure regarding critical test results, maintaining the patient's safety through communication to other patient care support staff during these procedures as appropriate. Identifies and assesses issues and opportunities for improvement and implements changes following managerial review. Follows up on action items to ensure completion. Contributes towards improving quality and safety scores on department scorecard.
Finance Essential Functions
Charges accurately for procedures, and logging the patient data. Submits all reports, billing and other paperwork within a timely manner. Uses resources efficiently; does not waste supplies. Ensures inventories of major supplies are never depleted. Self-motivated to independently manage time effectively and prioritize daily tasks, minimizing incidental overtime.
Growth/Innovation Essential Functions
Continues to learn and apply intermediate to advanced EEG and/or EP signal recognition, relevant medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, contraindications for activation procedures, instrumentation and preparation for use. Trains in END procedures. Offers innovative solutions through participation in performance improvement activities. Completes and updates the individual development plan (IDP) on an on-going basis.
This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive; the employee will also perform other reasonably related business/job duties as assigned. [Company name masked] reserves the right to revise job duties and responsibilities as the need arises.
cond_0301.requirements:
Must have one of the following: High School diploma or equivalent education (examples include: GED, verification of homeschool equivalency, partial or full completion of post-secondary education, etc.), Completion of an Accredited Electroneurodiagnostic (END) program, or Associate's degree or higher in a science related field from an accredited college or university
Two years experience in IOM procedures

When not scheduled for an IOM case, the Senior IOM Technologist may be asked to perform ambulatory and long term monitoring (LTM) electroencephalograms (EEG), and/or visual, brainstem, and somatosensory evoked potential (EP) procedures and/or monitor epilepsy patients according to hospital and departmental policy and procedures. This position delivers exceptional patient care per guidelines established by the department to ensure optimal patient safety and customer service and practices Patient and Family-Centered Care.
cond_0316.responsibilities:
People Essential Functions
Ensures understanding by the patient and staff the purpose of the procedures and answers questions regarding the procedures. Identifies and anticipates potential problems, communicates appropriately and effectively concerns to appropriate management; addresses issues as instructed, responding professionally at all times, and reports resolutions. Role models' healthy work relationships such as mitigation of conflict, leading problem-solving and resolution efforts. Anticipates needs of other team members; proactively offers assistance and promotes a positive work environment that actively assists interprofessional care team to achieve optimal department results. Serves as preceptor, mentor, and resource to less experience staff. Provides technical expertise to peers and/or non-credentialed team members as appropriate. Recommends initiatives to improve department scores for employee engagement on department scorecard.
Service Essential Functions
Independently conducts patient assessments. Recognizes and teaches peers drug and physiological status effects on activity monitored. In addition to performing all IOM modalities, independently performs EEG monitoring during: Wada, PET, ictal SPECT studies, ABRs, Phase Reversal and cortical mapping with indirect supervision as appropriate. Conducts intermediate to advanced technical troubleshooting and artifact identification and elimination; understands and follows concepts of digital equipment and electrical safety with regards to the equipment. Shares understanding with peers of EEG technology and its uses in the epilepsy monitoring unit as well as during epilepsy surgery. Independently monitors epilepsy monitoring patients. Independently performs EP studies or other EEG studies as assigned when there are no scheduled IOM cases. Role models behaviors and skills, through peer-to-peer accountability, towards improving department score for patient satisfaction.
Quality/Safety Essential Functions
Identifies clinically significant events and follows policy and procedure regarding critical test results, maintaining the patient's safety through communication to other patient care support staff during these procedures as appropriate. Identifies and assesses issues and opportunities for improvement and implements changes following managerial review. Follows up on action items to ensure completion. Contributes towards improving quality and safety scores on department scorecard.
Finance Essential Functions
Charges accurately for procedures, and logging the patient data. Submits all reports, billing and other paperwork within a timely manner. Uses resources efficiently; does not waste supplies. Ensures inventories of major supplies are never depleted. Self-motivated to independently manage time effectively and prioritize daily tasks, minimizing incidental overtime.
Growth/Innovation Essential Functions
Continues to learn and apply intermediate to advanced EEG and/or EP signal recognition, relevant medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, contraindications for activation procedures, instrumentation and preparation for use. Trains in END procedures. Offers innovative solutions through participation in performance improvement activities. Completes and updates the individual development plan (IDP) on an on-going basis.
This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive; the employee will also perform other reasonably related business/job duties as assigned. [Company name masked] reserves the right to revise job duties and responsibilities as the need arises.
cond_0316.requirements:
Must have one of the following: High School diploma or equivalent education (examples include: GED, verification of homeschool equivalency, partial or full completion of post-secondary education, etc.), Completion of an Accredited Electroneurodiagnostic (END) program, or Associate's degree or higher in a science related field from an accredited college or university
Two years experience in IOM procedures
cond_0316.values: We value excellence, focus, and the ability to produce strong outcomes. We believe organizations succeed when they hold themselves to a high bar.
cond_0316.workplace_support: We foster connection and community through employee groups and inclusive workplace initiatives so people can bring their full selves to work and find support across different identities and life experiences.

cond_0403.intro: The Senior Intraoperative Neuromonitoring (IOM) Technologist is responsible for performing neurodiagnostic procedures in the intraoperative monitoring field and all IOM modalities required as a registered neurodiagnostic technologist. This position independently performs IOM modalities including SSEPs, TceMEP, EMG (including triggered), ABRs, Phase Reversal, and cortical mapping. When not scheduled for an IOM case, the Senior IOM Technologist may be assigned to perform ambulatory and long-term monitoring (LTM) electroencephalograms (EEG), visual, brainstem, and somatosensory evoked potential (EP) procedures, and/or monitor epilepsy patients according to hospital and departmental policy and procedures. This position delivers patient care per guidelines established by the department to ensure patient safety and practices Patient and Family-Centered Care.
cond_0403.responsibilities:
People Essential Functions
Ensures the patient and staff understand the purpose of procedures and addresses questions about them.
Identifies and anticipates potential problems; communicates concerns to appropriate management, addresses issues as instructed, responds professionally, and documents resolutions.
Models healthy work relationships including conflict mitigation and problem-solving.
Anticipates needs of other team members; offers assistance as needed and supports a positive work environment that helps the interprofessional care team achieve department results.
Serves as preceptor, mentor, and resource to less experienced staff.
Provides technical guidance to peers and non-credentialed team members as appropriate.
Recommends initiatives to improve department employee engagement scores.
Service Essential Functions
Independently conducts patient assessments.
Recognizes and explains to peers the effects of drug and physiological status on monitored activity.
In addition to performing all IOM modalities, independently performs EEG monitoring during Wada, PET, ictal SPECT studies, ABRs, Phase Reversal, and cortical mapping with indirect supervision as appropriate.
Conducts intermediate to advanced technical troubleshooting and artifact identification and elimination; understands and follows concepts of digital equipment and electrical safety.
Shares knowledge of EEG technology and its uses in the epilepsy monitoring unit and during epilepsy surgery with peers.
Independently monitors epilepsy monitoring patients.
Independently performs EP studies or other EEG studies as assigned when no IOM cases are scheduled.
Models behaviors and skills through peer-to-peer accountability toward improving department patient satisfaction scores.
Quality/Safety Essential Functions
Identifies clinically significant events and follows policy and procedure regarding critical test results, maintaining patient safety through communication to relevant patient care support staff during procedures as appropriate.
Identifies issues and opportunities for improvement and implements changes following managerial review.
Follows up on action items to ensure completion.
Contributes toward improving quality and safety scores on the department scorecard.
Finance Essential Functions
Charges accurately for procedures and logs patient data.
Submits all reports, billing, and other paperwork in a timely manner.
Uses resources efficiently and avoids wasting supplies.
Ensures inventories of major supplies are not depleted.
Independently manages time effectively and prioritizes daily tasks, minimizing incidental overtime.
Growth/Innovation Essential Functions
Continues to develop intermediate to advanced EEG and/or EP signal recognition, relevant medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, contraindications for activation procedures, instrumentation, and preparation for use.
Trains in END procedures.
Contributes to performance improvement activities.
Completes and updates the individual development plan (IDP) on an ongoing basis.
This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive; the employee will also perform other reasonably related business/job duties as assigned. [Company name masked] reserves the right to revise job duties and responsibilities as the need arises.
cond_0403.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
One of the following: High School diploma or equivalent education (examples include: GED, verification of homeschool equivalency, partial or full completion of post-secondary education, etc.), completion of an Accredited Electroneurodiagnostic (END) program, or Associate's degree or higher in a science-related field from an accredited college or university.
Two years of experience in IOM procedures.
Preferred Requirements
Credential as a registered neurodiagnostic technologist.
